summary: A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Gyurme Dorje studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1968–1971) and SOAS (PhD ~1981–1987) under Philip Denwood and several traditional teachers. He later served as a research fellow at SOAS (~1991–2002).

Specializing in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, György Hazai studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1949–1954). He held a post at the German Academy of Sciences at Berlin from circa 1963 to 1982.
György Kara specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1953–1958) and held a post at Indiana University from ~1993 to 2022.

An Indologist, Gérard Colas held posts at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique as Directeur de recherche (attested 2004) and Senior Fellow (attested 2009), and at the École des hautes études en sciences sociales (attested 2012).

Gérard Fussman worked in Indology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at École Normale Supérieure (~1960–1964), he succeeded Jean Filliozat and held a professorship at the Collège de France (~1984–2011, attested 2012).

A scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Central Asian studies, Bethlenfalvy studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1956–1963) under Louis Ligeti. He held posts at the University of Delhi (1970), Eötvös Loránd University (~1990–2005), and the University of Vienna (2007–2008).
Gösta Liebert worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils M. Holmer, and Stig Wikander. He served on the faculty at the University of Gothenburg from circa 1956 to 1982.

A historian and archaeologist, Götz von Selle studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1913–1914), the University of Kiel, and the University of Göttingen (~1917–1920). He held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1924 to 1956.
Specializing in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Günter Grönbold served at the Bavarian State Library from circa 1974 to 2008, where he was Head of the South Asia Department.

Active in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Günter Schweiger studied at the Vienna University of Economics and Business (~1961–1966) and under Gert Klingenschmitt (~1995–2006). He held a post at the Vienna University of Economics and Business (~1974–2009).

An Indologist, H. G. Narahari studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras, where C. Kunhan Raja supervised his MA (1939). In 1944, he was attested as a Research Fellow at Madras and Research Assistant at Adyar Library.
Specializing in Indology and philosophy, H. V. Nagaraja Rao held a post at the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore, and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).
A scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, Hachiro Hasebe studied at Keio University (~1969–1978) and held an assistant professor post at Komazawa University from circa 1993 to 2000.
Haeju Sunim works in Buddhist studies. She served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and was attested as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Dongguk University in 1999.

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, she completed an MA at Peking University (-1982) under Kemu Jin and studied under Zhongxin Jiang. She held posts at the University of Vienna (attested 1996) and University of Freiburg (2010, attested 2013).

A linguist and Tibetologist, Kitamura studied at Tokyo University (~1944–1948) under Tokan Tada. He worked at NINJAL (~1951–1964), Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1964–1986), Reitaku University (~1986–1994), and directed the Centre for East Asian Cultural Studies (~1987–1991).

An Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar, Nakamura studied at the University of Tokyo (1936), later serving as professor there (1943–1973). He was a visiting professor at Stanford (1951–1952) and directed the Eastern Institute and Toho Gakuin (~1973–1999).

Active in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy, Okayama studied at the University of Tokyo (~1975–1978) and under Xianlin Ji (~1980–1982). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1988–2013) and Chūō Bukkyō Gakuin (~2013–2022).

An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Sakurabe studied at Otani University (PhD 1944–1967) under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi. He taught at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1955–1958) and held long-term academic appointments at Otani University from 1949 to 1996.

A philosopher, Hajime Tanabe studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1908) and Kyoto University, studying under Kitaro Nishida (~1914–1928). He held academic posts at Tohoku University (~1913–1919) and Kyoto University (~1919–1945).
